gen_risks.description: Sector utilities face growing financial deficits because current electricity prices remain below the cost of service, threatening sector sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support government tariff reform strategies and analytical studies on utility financial viability during implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: financial deficit in the sector could reach 36 percent of system costs by the end of 2025.

gen_risks.description: Project funds flow may experience delays and administrative bottlenecks due to Treasury single account requirements for local currency transactions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Collaborate closely with MOF and MOE and establish a dedicated Treasury Operating sub-account for PMO incremental operating costs.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays and bottlenecks in the project funds flow arrangements that got complicated with the addition of an investment project account within the Treasury

gen_risks.description: Local market supply of civil works and construction materials risks failing quality standards required for 220kV transmission lines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate rated criteria into international competitive bidding to evaluate material quality control strategies and non-price technical criteria.
gen_risks.evidence: 40% of construction materials were found unqualified in the local market.

gen_risks.description: The dominance of aging, inflexible coal-fired CHP units limits system flexibility and complicates variable renewable energy integration.
gen_risks.mitigation: Reinforce transmission corridor capacity and redundancy while integrating battery energy storage systems and long-term grid integration planning.
gen_risks.evidence: Most of the CHP units are aging (the youngest one is more than 40 years old), inefficient and highly polluting.

gen_risks.description: Mongolia's short construction season creates severe schedule compression, where failure to finish civil works before winter causes year-long delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct advance procurement and apply rated evaluation criteria assessing contractors' technical approaches for short construction window optimization.
gen_risks.evidence: If it cannot be completed before winter, the Project will have more delays with waiting for the next construction season.

gen_risks.description: The newly established PMO may lack initial familiarity with World Bank operational, financial management, and procurement procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint qualified PMO staff prior to effectiveness, provide specialized World Bank training, and recruit an Owner's Engineer for implementation support.
gen_risks.evidence: Given new PMO FM staff may be lack of prior experience with and knowledge of procedures regarding Bank-financed projects

gen_risks.description: Evaluation Committee members may lack experience handling English-language procurement documents, causing evaluation delays on international tenders.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver early procurement training to Evaluation Committee members and engage consultant support for complex international competitive selections.
gen_risks.evidence: Evaluation Committee members normally do not have knowledge and experience in handling English documents, and it may cause delays

gen_risks.description: High-level political interference in procurement decision-making could lead to evaluation delays and compromised procurement integrity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Clearly define decision-making workflows and delegation of authority in the Project Operational Manual and strictly enforce World Bank prior reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Interference of the high-level officials in procurement decision making which leads to delays.

gen_risks.description: National election cycles may trigger institutional turnover among government officials and key PMO/MOE staff, disrupting implementation continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage proactively with incoming government officials and document operational procedures comprehensively in the Project Operational Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential changes in Government officials involved in project activities due to election cycle... and possible impact on MOE and PMO FM staffing.

gen_risks.description: Overhead transmission lines present collision and electrocution hazards to local bird species and avifauna populations during operation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Realign transmission line routes away from sensitive wetlands and install bird-friendly features such as flight diverters under a Bird Management Plan.
gen_risks.evidence: disruption including bird collision risk, exposure to EMF, workers health and OHS

gen_risks.description: Extreme cold, freezing conditions, heavy snow, and high winds pose risks of damage or failure to transmission towers and infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply enhanced structural engineering standards for high wind loading, rated extreme design temperatures, and improved insulator designs.
gen_risks.evidence: exposure to drought and extreme cold identified as the strongest drivers of risk.

gen_risks.description: Heavy reliance on imported construction materials and specialized transmission components exposes the project to border delays and price volatility.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early market intelligence, initiate advance procurement for long-lead specialized equipment, and monitor supply chain risks continuously.
gen_risks.evidence: 75-80% of construction materials are sourced from outside the country

gen_risks.description: Transmission line construction works may temporarily restrict local herders' access to pasture, water wells, and community resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Resettlement Policy Framework and Stakeholder Engagement Plan while maintaining an active two-stage Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: temporary restriction of access to resources by local herders (for example, pasture, wells, etc.)

gen_risks.description: Gender-based biases and structural obstacles in sector entities hinder female employment and career advancement into technical and managerial roles.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a workplace gender gap assessment, establish gender-responsive HR policies, offer leadership training for women, and monitor target gender metrics.
gen_risks.evidence: gender-based biases may be an obstacle to women's employment and especially to career progression at NPTG.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risks are rated Substantial. The parliamentary election was held in June 2024 and a new coalition government was formed, with representation of all three major political parties. While there may be risks of disagreement on the approval of individual projects, these risks will be mitigated by the strong alignment of the proposed operation with the NRP and the new Government Action Plan for 2024-2028.
gt_risks.mitigation: Continued engagement with key stakeholders, including government and the parliament, through ongoing analytical and technical support on VRE integration and energy sector reform, will help mitigate risks going forward. The Development Partner Group, co-chaired by the World Bank and UNDP, will also offer a donor coordination platform to maintain political momentum for RE integration.

gt_risks.description: The macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. Mongolia's economic outlook is dependent on global macroeconomic factors, in particular commodity prices. Despite recent positive short-term developments from coal and agricultural exports, Mongolia still needs to strengthen fiscal and external buffers to respond to future shocks and continue reforms aimed at diversifying the economy.
gt_risks.mitigation: To mitigate these risks and manage external balances, the World Bank has been, and will continue to be, supporting the authorities in restoring fiscal and external buffers through analytical and advisory work.

gt_risks.description: The sector strategies and policies risk is rated Substantial. Substantial risk still exists due to institutional fragmentation, lack of policies to promote RE projects, and lack of clear commitment of reforms, especially related to tariff reforms that are crucial to make the sector viable and be able to refinance projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include actively engaging in multi-stakeholder coordination meetings and providing technical advice and capacity building to key stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: The institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk is rated Substantial. The implementing agency MOE and NPTG have experience implementing World Bank-funded projects; however, there is a substantial risk that newly hired PMO staff may not have sufficient capacity, which could potentially lead to implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The PMO will be strengthened with experienced consultants and targeted training and capacity building. Mitigating measures include the World Bank's scrutiny of PMO members' selection, including a review of the TOR and providing no objection to the qualification criteria of the staff.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. There are substantial risks due to the reliance of MOE on a newly constituted PMO, which may cause delays in processing payments, conducting IFRs, and other reporting requirements; the construction sector in Mongolia is often subject to delays and cost overruns. Potential procurement risks include (i) likelihood of time and cost overruns due to weak contract management capacity, and (ii) significant procurement delays due to delayed initiation of procurement and establishment of needed staffing arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: Capacity building through customized training and TA is a central element of the Project, along with strong project supervision and contract management capacity building; MOE will continue to directly provide intensive support to the PMO. Procurement risks are mitigated by (a) establishing a PMO with appropriate procurement and technical staff per FIDIC contract standards; (b) clearly defined workflow in decision-making within the MOE/PMO procurement manual; and (c) extensive market engagement to stimulate market participation.
